text.p: Italian bonds and Btp futures closed steadily firmer but off session highs, continuing the rally seen in futures on hopes of an early Bank of Italy interest rate cut.

"The market's attention at the moment is on the Bank of Italy. Every day's a good day for a rate cut and every day that passes increases the probability that it will happen the following day," one trader said.

Operators said that forecasts by Italian employers' body Confindustria for perhaps zero growth in first quarter GDP and that CPI may fall to 1.5 pervcent this month were "supportive" for the market but already more or less priced in.

The 10-year February 1, 2007 cash bond ended 22 basis points up at 96.34 with the spread over bunds narrowing to 162 bps from 165. The June Btp Liffe future contract overcame resistance at 129.00 early on and touched a session high of 129.35.
Some traders saw little concrete signs of selling and said the rally could continue up to 130.00 with a return below 129.00 being the first sign of weakness.
They said the fact the Btp futures had managed to maintain the rally despite weakness on other markets like T-bonds and bunds was seen as very positive.
